title: ci(pm): adopt the board-snapshot archiver — route B, and the five files this repo's own gates demanded (objectui#9387)
body:
Fixes #9387

objectui now has a board archive. `scripts/pm/board-snapshot.mjs` and `.github/workflows/board-snapshot.yml` are adopted from objectstack; the archiver loads, self-tests and reads **this** board, measured below.

⭐ **The card said two files and "there is nothing to configure". It took seven, and five of them were named by a gate in this repository rather than by the adopt section.** That is the most useful thing this card produces for the next sibling that adopts, so it is the first table rather than a footnote.

| # | file | who demanded it |
|--:|:--|:--|
| 1 | `scripts/pm/board-snapshot.mjs` | the card |
| 2 | `.github/workflows/board-snapshot.yml` | the card |
| 3 | `scripts/pm/check-half-states.mjs` | the archiver's own `import`, at module load — `SyntaxError`, before its first predicate |
| 4 | `scripts/upstream-port-pin.json` | `check:upstream-port-parity`: 3 is a pinned port, and both new files are ports nothing watched |
| 5 | `scripts/dependabot-merge-gate.mjs` | `dependabot-merge-gate.test.ts`: every check a `pull_request` workflow produces must be classified |
| 6 | `content/docs/guide/ci-cd-pipeline.md` | `ci-cd-pipeline-doc.test.ts`: every workflow owes an inventory row, a section, and every first-party command it runs |
| 7 | `scripts/__tests__/upstream-port-parity-wiring.test.ts` | its own back leg, once 4 put a second ported program under `scripts/pm/` |

⚠️ The general lesson, stated plainly rather than as a complaint: **the adopt cost is not a file count, it is whatever the adopting repository's own gates demand**, and the source repository cannot enumerate that. Upstream's adopt section is not wrong about its own tree; it is answering a question only the destination can answer.

## Route B, and the honesty clause that comes with it

The archiver imports five symbols from `scripts/pm/check-half-states.mjs`. This tree exported three: `PROXY_FLAG` and `proxyRearmPlan` were absent, and that is not an accident — this repository's copy of the sweeper is a **pinned port**, pinned to objectstack `bf10debd5`, and that ref carries **zero** occurrences of `PROXY_FLAG`. The proxy re-exec plan landed upstream after the pin was taken.

The maintainer ruled **route B**: declare the block as a twelfth divergence on the existing pin, rather than re-syncing the port (roughly 23,000 lines of upstream change) or forking the plan into the archiver.

**What landed.** The 90-line block — `PROXY_FLAG`, `PROXY_REARM_GUARD`, `proxyRoute` and `proxyRearmPlan`, with their doc comment — taken verbatim from objectstack `eec56c37dfc89086658c1659bb2da869dfa08d4f`, grafted into the ported sweeper directly after `EXIT_PREREQUISITE_NOT_MET`, and declared as divergence `proxy-rearm-plan` whose `why` reads, in part:

> ⚠️ THIS ENTRY ADDS UPSTREAM CODE THAT POSTDATES THE PIN — it does not adapt pinned code, which every other divergence here does, and it makes this port a deliberate SUPERSET of the ref it is pinned at. […] ⛔ ON THE NEXT RE-SYNC, DELETE THIS ENTRY rather than carrying it forward: once upstream's own bytes contain the block, applying this divergence forward inserts a SECOND copy and the duplicate export fails loudly at load.

⭐ **The question route B does not answer, left visible here on purpose.** The maintainer picked B for its blast radius. ⛔ That is a decision about SCOPE, not a ruling that this gate's contract permits a divergence to **add** rather than **adapt** — every other entry in the pin adapts. Whoever owns `check:upstream-port-parity` should still rule on whether the superset relationship is allowed, and the divergence's own `why` says so where the next reader of the port will meet it.

## The two red shards, both causes read

**Shard 2/8 — `dependabot-merge-gate.test.ts`.** The PR leg produces a new check name that classified into none of the three buckets. `REQUIRED_CONTEXTS` admits only contexts whose workflow carries **no** path filter, and this one has a `paths:` list ⇒ it cannot be required. It is now in **`OPTIONAL_CONTEXTS`**, modelled on `Hook Self-Tests`:

> `board-snapshot.yml` filters on paths: `scripts/pm/board-snapshot.mjs`, `scripts/pm/check-half-states.mjs`, `scripts/invoked-as.mjs`, plus the workflow file itself (objectui#9387). Blocking when it runs: the `pull_request` leg runs the archiver's own `--self-test` and then a capped `--dry-run` snapshot on a real runner, so an archiver that cannot load is red before it merges. It is OPTIONAL rather than required because that path filter means it does not report at all on a pull request touching none of those four files, which is every Dependabot bump. ⛔ Not `NOT_A_GATE`: that bucket says a check cannot gate, and this one is the only thing in the repository that exercises the archiver before it merges.

**Shard 5/8 — `ci-cd-pipeline-doc.test.ts`, three assertions, one root cause.** Not the same census as shard 2/8. Every workflow in `.github/workflows/` owes a section headed ``### Title (`name.yml`)`` on `content/docs/guide/ci-cd-pipeline.md` **and** a row in its Workflow Inventory table; a third assertion then sweeps each section for command parity. `board-snapshot.yml` had neither. It now has both, and one detail is worth naming because it is a trap: the sweep treats a single-quoted path as data and an unquoted one as a command, so a section that writes a path list unquoted is read as claiming its workflow runs those gates. The trigger paragraph quotes the `paths:` entries the way the YAML does. A first draft also named the parity gate as `pnpm check:…` and was refused as a phantom — the page may not credit a workflow with a gate it does not run — so the section names that gate and says where it runs instead.

**Third failure, caused by the pin registration rather than found on the old head.** `upstream-port-parity-wiring.test.ts` asserted that every pinned file under `scripts/pm/` appears in the **half-state patrol's** `pull_request.paths`. That heuristic read `scripts/pm/` as a synonym for "the patrol's unit", which was true while the sweeper was the only program there. ⛔ Adding the archiver to the patrol's filter would have been the wrong repair: the patrol does not load the archiver, and declaring it would run the patrol on pull requests that cannot affect it. The back leg now asks each pinned program **which** workflow watches it, and still asserts by name that the sweeper's answer is this patrol. The file had already been re-scoped once for the same class of reason, which is recorded in its own comment.

⚠️ An earlier version of that repair walked `.github/workflows/` and tripped an eighth census — `markdown-test-inputs.test.ts` adjudicates tests that walk a directory. The landed version uses a named map instead, so a third ported program under `scripts/pm/` costs a deliberate line here rather than being absorbed silently.

## Premises, re-taken on `804831c2a`

| premise | reading |
|:--|:--|
| objectui `scripts/pm/board-snapshot.mjs` | ABSENT |
| objectui `.github/workflows/board-snapshot.yml` | ABSENT |
| objectui `refs/heads/board-archive` | 0 refs |
| objectui `scripts/pm/check-half-states.mjs` | PRESENT — and missing two of the five exports the archiver imports |
| objectui `scripts/invoked-as.mjs` | PRESENT |
| objectstack `origin/main` `eec56c37d` | both source files PRESENT; the R2 step is in the workflow |

The card's declared blocker on objectstack#17989 is spent; the workflow adopted here is the post-R2 one.

## The cron measurement, and the decision

This repository's scheduled inventory, read with `grep -rn 'cron:' .github/workflows/` at `804831c2a`:

| workflow | cron | hours |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `changeset-release.yml` | `0 */6 * * *` | 0, 6, 12, 18 at :00 |
| `check-links.yml` | `17 4 * * 0` | Sundays 04:17 |
| `half-state-patrol.yml` | `37 1,7,13,19 * * *` | 1, 7, 13, 19 at :37 |
| `live-e2e.yml` | `30 6 * * *` | 06:30 |
| `merge-queue-head-patrol.yml` | `7,22,37,52 * * * *` | **EVERY hour**, four times |
| `node-esm-load-gate.yml` | `17 4 * * *` | 04:17 |
| `published-dist-gate.yml` | `41 3 * * *` | 03:41 |
| `required-check-set-patrol.yml` | `23 5 * * *` | 05:23 |
| `shadcn-check.yml` | `0 9 * * 1` | Mondays 09:00 |
| `spec-range-floors.yml` | `11 4 * * *` | 04:11 |

**Hours — `2,8,14,20` survives.** Upstream's method: stay out of the half-state patrol's hours, because both are heavy board readers against one per-repository-per-hour `GITHUB_TOKEN` budget; then take the least contended remaining set. Applied here, the patrol holds `1,7,13,19` and of the five six-hourly sets that avoid it, `2,8,14,20` is the **only** one whose four hours carry no other scheduled workflow at all. `0,6,12,18` meets the changeset release in all four hours; `3,9,15,21` carries 03:41 and Monday 09:00; `4,10,16,22` drops an 800-request run into the busiest hour on this board (04:11, 04:17, and 04:17 again on Sundays); `5,11,17,23` carries 05:23. Same answer as upstream, reached independently.

**Minute — `7` does NOT survive; it moves to `14`.** ⭐ This is the collision the source file's rationale cannot reach. Upstream reasons about **hours**, plus one sentence about staying off the top of the hour because "scheduled workflows queue behind everyone else's :00 cron". That sentence is an argument about minute contention — and this repository runs a merge-queue head patrol **every hour** at `7,22,37,52`. A verbatim `7 2,8,14,20` would start the archiver in the same minute as that patrol in all four of its hours. Upstream has no such hourly patrol, so its own measurement had nothing to trip on.

`14` is the midpoint of the first clear window after the top of the hour (:07 to :22), no cron in this repository uses minute 14, and it is early enough that this job's 15-minute timeout cannot spill its requests into the next hour's budget window — which `44`, the other roomy midpoint, cannot promise.

⇒ **`- cron: '14 2,8,14,20 * * *'`**

## What is pinned, and what diverges

`scripts/pm/board-snapshot.mjs` is **byte-identical** to objectstack `origin/main` (`ebd5beb5caaf18f5…`), so it pins at **0 divergences**. All divergence is in the workflow: **9 declared text pairs**, derived mechanically from the diff rather than transcribed, each widened with context until its anchor is unique on both sides, and proven to round-trip — forward reproduces the ported file byte for byte, reverse reproduces upstream byte for byte.

| id | what it is |
|:--|:--|
| `card-ref-header`, `card-ref-open-phase`, `card-ref-freshness` | bare objectstack card references repo-qualified; unqualified they read here as this repository's card numbers |
| `spender-inventory` | the shared-budget table is this repository's, and names the instrument that re-derives it |
| `pr-trigger-unenforced` | upstream cites `check:pm-dispatch-gates`, which mechanically requires the trigger **there**; this tree has no such gate, so the paragraph says the trigger is an unenforced convention here |
| `self-test-not-wired` | upstream names three instruments — a `check:*` self-test step, a required lint job, and the gate requiring that step — **none of which exists here**; the paragraph now states the consequence instead |
| `schedule` | the cron above |
| `r2-mirror-prefix`, `r2-tarball-prefix` | ⚠️ the one non-cosmetic divergence, below |

⭐ **The R2 prefix.** Upstream hard-codes `objectstack/` in the `--delete` sync target and in the daily tarball key, while everything else about *which* board is handled is passed in as `PM_SWEEP_REPO`. Two repositories aimed at one bucket with that literal would share a single `--delete` target: each run makes the prefix equal to *its* branch tip, so each board's run erases the other's objects, and the day's tarball is whichever board ran first. The result is a complete, well-formed, green archive that is half missing. A comment at the line says so and says not to restore the literal on a re-sync.

## What was measured

**① Route B landed — the archiver loads and self-tests in THIS tree.**

```
$ node scripts/pm/board-snapshot.mjs --self-test
exit 0
OK board-snapshot self-test: 156 cases pass across 12 batteries …

$ node scripts/pm/check-half-states.mjs --self-test
exit 0
✓ check-half-states self-test: 1574 cases pass.
```

**② The copy archives THIS board — verified from the archived bytes, not from the source comment's promise.**

```
$ PM_SWEEP_REPO=objectstack-ai/objectui node scripts/pm/board-snapshot.mjs \
    --out=OUTDIR --limit=5 --max-requests=25
exit 0
board-snapshot — objectstack-ai/objectui into OUTDIR
  phase     open — the open board first: the records a suspension destroys
  read      5 number(s) in 6 request(s); walk INCOMPLETE

$ node -e "console.log(require('OUTDIR/manifest.json').repo)"
objectstack-ai/objectui
$ node -e "console.log(require('OUTDIR/issues/2763.json').html_url)"
https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectui/issues/2763
```

The `html_url` is the proof: the archived record is an objectui issue.

**③ The resolver refuses rather than falling back.** Both legs fire, both exit non-zero — unset resolves to `default` and is refused with the "archive of the wrong board" paragraph; `PM_SWEEP_REPO='not-a-repo'` is refused as not `owner/name`. ⭐ Worth stating plainly: in **this** repository `DEFAULT_SWEEP_REPO` is already `objectstack-ai/objectui`, so the default would have been harmless here. The refusal fires on the *source* being `default` regardless of its value, which is what makes the guard hold for the next sibling rather than only for the lucky one.

**④ The R2 step, all three legs.**

| leg | result |
|:--|:--|
| all four secrets unset | **exit 0**, one `::notice::`, `status=skipped — no R2 credentials configured in this repository` |
| one of four set | **exit 0**, same skip — the guard is an OR over all four |
| all four set, upload fails | **exit 1**, `::error::aws s3 sync to R2 exited 127`, `status=FAILED` |

⇒ the card's claim 4 holds in the copied file: this lands green with no secrets, and a *configured* upload that breaks goes red instead of going quiet. Setting the four values stays a maintainer action on repository settings; nothing here touches a secret value.

**⑤ The `paths:` list is complete for this layout.** Derived mechanically: `board-snapshot.mjs` imports `../invoked-as.mjs` and `./check-half-states.mjs`; `check-half-states.mjs` imports `../invoked-as.mjs`; `invoked-as.mjs` is a leaf. The closure is exactly three files, the list is those three plus the workflow, and all four exist here at the spelled paths.

**⑥ Ablation — the re-scoped wiring assertion can still fail.** Deleting `'scripts/pm/board-snapshot.mjs'` from the workflow's own `paths:` was written to disk (blob `b5c483fba` → `2971ef45f`, injected-text count 0 confirmed by grep), the suite went red at the exact line the repair added, and the restore was verified by hash equality back to `b5c483fba`, not by an exit code.

```
MUTATED RUN EXIT=1
 FAIL  upstream-port-parity-wiring.test.ts > the patrol's own ported unit is pinned, in both directions
    145|       expect(wf.on.pull_request.paths).toContain(program);
```

## First run: none yet, and the card is wrong to ask for one before merge

⛔ No run created `board-archive`, and none could. `GET /repos/objectstack-ai/objectui/actions/workflows` returns `total_count` 51 with 51 entries — a complete enumeration — and no entry for `board-snapshot`. **GitHub registers a workflow for `workflow_dispatch` only once the file exists on the default branch**, so no pre-merge run is possible from a topic branch, for this or any other new workflow.

⇒ what creates `board-archive` is the **first scheduled fire after merge, at the next `14 2,8,14,20` slot** (or a manual dispatch from the Actions tab, available once the file is on `main`). That run gets named in a follow-up comment on the card. ⛔ No run is claimed here, and the pull request is not held for one that cannot happen.

## Acceptance notes

- There is no behavioural pin to write for a copied workflow and none was invented. The archiver's behaviour travels with the file in its own `--self-test`; what this repository asserts about the adoption is ① to ⑥ above plus the twenty gates.
- ⛔ `lint.yml` was **not** touched. Upstream holds the archiver's self-test in a required lint job with no paths filter; neither that step nor the gate requiring it exists here, so the self-test is reachable only behind this workflow's own `paths:` filter, and a change that breaks the archiver while touching none of those four files merges unexercised. The copied header says this out loud. Wiring it in is a follow-up card.
- The 18 lines in `board-snapshot.mjs` carrying bare `#NNNN` references to objectstack cards are untouched on purpose: the file pins at 0 divergences, and declaring eighteen cosmetic text pairs would trade a free re-sync for nothing.
- `scripts/pm/board-snapshot.mjs` and the sweeper are now both pinned, so a future objectstack change to either is a red `check:upstream-port-parity` rather than silent drift.

Clause-②: no
